newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Labour regains 20-point poll lead.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Labour regains 20-point poll lead.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour Party has regained its 20-point opinion poll lead over the ruling Conservatives after seeing its popularity dip during October, according to the latest poll.

The NOP poll for the Sunday Times newspaper showed Labour with 50 percent support, up three points from a month ago, while Prime Minister John Major's Conservatives were down three points at 30 percent.
The Conservatives have been in power since 1979, but have consistently lagged Labour in polls for the past two years. Major must call an election by May 1997.

Recent opinion polls have shown Labour with leads over the Conservatives varying from 15 to 29 points. The polls show different levels of support according to the questions asked and how polling organisations adjust their raw figures.
The latest NOP poll gave the minority Liberal Democrats 15 percent of the vote, down one point from a month ago.
